answer: An agent market serving quartz mines, mesa farms, and jetty operators requires each identity to lock a fixed bond for 30 days before submitting bids, with one active bid allowed per bond. Creating extra names grants no extra bidding capacity unless each name posts fresh capital. An attacker seeking 1,000 simultaneous bids must therefore immobilize 1,000 bonds, bearing financing costs and losing access to that money throughout the lockup.
